solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Left-leaning material used by writer on power (4)

indicators.note: in an across clue, INK placed 'on' P comes after it

blocks.note: P is the symbol for power

annotation.surface: A writer drafting on a political theme uses left-wing material.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Pink' is a mild word for someone with left-wing sympathies, a paler shade of red.
annotation.definitionFit: Pink describes a person whose politics lean moderately to the left.

entries.clue: Means to devalue company’s reason for producing fewer Teletubbies? (6,4)

blocks.note: a tactic a company uses to make itself less valuable to a hostile bidder
a cryptic reading: what would stop one Teletubby having babies? Split the letters into four short words

annotation.surface: A children's TV franchise wonders why the company is making fewer Teletubby toys.
annotation.walkthrough: The Teletubbies are a British children's TV show whose four characters include Po. Split the answer as PO IS ON PILL and the joke appears; the question mark flags the pun.
annotation.definitionFit: A poison pill is a defence that lowers a company's value to deter a takeover.

entries.clue: American right-wingers in Colorado blocking gas supply’s introduction (3-4)

indicators.note: 'in Colorado' tells you Colorado's abbreviation is the piece placed inside another word
CO sits inside NEON, blocking it
a word's introduction is its first letter

blocks.note: CO is the postal abbreviation for Colorado

annotation.surface: Conservative Americans in Colorado hold up the start of a gas supply.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'in Colorado' as a location, but it is an insertion: the state's abbreviation goes inside the gas.
annotation.definitionFit: Neo-cons, short for neoconservatives, are a hawkish faction of the American right.

entries.clue: They plan school education regulations; Republican pushed back (10)

indicators.note: the R of RULES is moved further back in the word

blocks.note: RULES with its R moved back three places

annotation.surface: A Republican drive to reverse school education rules meets planners in a political row.
annotation.walkthrough: The semicolon makes 'Republican pushed back' look like a separate news item, but it instructs moving the R of RULES further along the word.
annotation.definitionFit: Schedulers are people who plan timetables.

entries.clue: Gold toilet covers for officer in command (9)

indicators.note: the toilet goes round the gold

blocks.note: a chair containing a chamber pot

annotation.surface: A commanding officer is given a gold-covered toilet as a perk.
annotation.walkthrough: OR for gold comes from heraldry.
annotation.definitionFit: A commodore is a naval officer who commands a squadron.

entries.clue: King of Northumbria drank alcohol when cycling (5)

indicators.note: the letters rotate, the end ED moving to the front

blocks.note: wined, as in wined and dined

annotation.surface: An Anglo-Saxon king went drinking while out on a bicycle.
annotation.walkthrough: Cycling a word moves letters from one end to the other: WIN|ED becomes ED|WIN.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Edwin ruled Northumbria in the seventh century and was its first Christian king.

entries.clue: Rack and ruin of Bermudan stall (8,5)

indicators.note: the letters of BERMUDAN STALL are wrecked and rebuilt

annotation.surface: A market stall in Bermuda has gone to rack and ruin.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Rack and ruin' is a fixed phrase, so it hides that 'Rack' alone is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the hallway stand where wet umbrellas are propped is a kind of rack.

entries.clue: Chained up spiny anteater (7)

indicators.note: as in 'things are up', disturbed

annotation.surface: A spiny anteater has been chained up.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Chained up' reads as one phrase; 'up' is what stirs the letters.
annotation.definitionFit: The echidna is an egg-laying spiny anteater of Australia and New Guinea.

entries.clue: Son had food glut (4)

annotation.surface: A son ate far too much.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Glut' looks like a noun summing up the meal, but it is the verb: to glut is to fill to excess.
annotation.definitionFit: To glut and to sate both mean to fill beyond need.

entries.clue: One very in favour of medium protein variant (7)

blocks.note: to be for something is to favour it

annotation.surface: Someone strongly supports a middling version of a protein.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Medium' seems to describe the protein but is just the size label on clothing; the definition is a technical biology term.
annotation.definitionFit: An isoform is one of several slightly different forms of the same protein.

entries.clue: Keep principal male in a certain commercial’s final shot? (3,3,3,4)

indicators.note: FORT and HERO go inside ONE…AD

blocks.note: as in 'one Mr Smith', a certain Mr Smith
a keep is a castle's stronghold
the male lead of a story

annotation.surface: An advert's leading man is retained for its closing camera shot.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Shot' suggests filming, but here it is a shot of drink; the question mark flags the play.
annotation.definitionFit: One for the road is a last drink before leaving, so a final shot.

entries.clue: You and I start to believe church engaged in online discussion (7)

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: you and I together are we

annotation.surface: Two people begin to believe the church is joining an internet debate.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Engaged in' looks like a container instruction but gives AT, as in 'at play'.
annotation.definitionFit: A webchat is a conversation held over the internet.

entries.clue: Missing company boss is at personal risk (2,4,3,4)

annotation.surface: A company's absent chief executive is putting themself in danger.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Missing company' looks like a business that has vanished; it means lacking companions.
annotation.definitionFit: If something is on your own head, you alone bear the risk or blame.

entries.clue: Divided Easter egg supply with daughter (10)

indicators.note: read as the adverb of supple: bendily, flexibly

annotation.surface: An Easter egg stock is shared out with a daughter.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Supply' looks like a noun, a stock of eggs, but is supple turned into an adverb (supplely), telling you to bend the letters.
annotation.definitionFit: Segregated means separated or divided into groups.

entries.clue: Poet’s reimagined Italian sauce (5)

indicators.note: the letters are imagined afresh in a new order

annotation.surface: A poet puts a creative spin on an Italian sauce.
annotation.walkthrough: The apostrophe-s is ignored: only the five letters of POETS are rearranged.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: pesto, the basil and pine-nut sauce from Genoa, is one Italian sauce among many.

entries.clue: Revolutionary metallic solar screens swing to and fro (9)

indicators.note: a revolution turns the text around
the phrase hides the answer inside it

blocks.note: the nine letters from the E of metallic to the O of solar

annotation.surface: Rebel metal solar panels are swaying about.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' seems to describe the panels, but it tells you to read backwards.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a pendulum oscillates, moving regularly one way then the other.

entries.clue: Rhythmic music from, say, Liverpool and Birmingham football club? (4,5)

indicators.note: Liverpool is given as one example of a city

blocks.note: Liverpool is an example of a city
Birmingham City FC's nickname is the Blues

annotation.surface: A chant heard in the stands of two English football grounds.
annotation.walkthrough: Birmingham City is an English football club nicknamed the Blues for its blue kit.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by genre: the urban, band-backed blues of Chicago and other cities has a strong rhythm section.

entries.clue: Drunk welcoming former serviceman with little post on social media (4-5)

indicators.note: LIT takes in the other pieces
'with' means accompanied by, so the little word travels alongside the ex-serviceman into the drunk

annotation.surface: A drunk befriends an ex-soldier, then fires off a short message online.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Wee' is Scottish for small, and 'little post' seems to describe the social-media message, but 'little' belongs to the wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: To live-tweet is to post running updates on social media as an event happens.

entries.clue: How group of geese fly over plain (7)

indicators.note: in a down clue, the phrase is turned over, bottom to top

blocks.note: all in a V, the formation a skein of geese flies in

annotation.surface: A question about how a flock of geese crosses a stretch of flatland.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Plain' looks like the land the geese cross, but it is the definition; 'over' turns ALL IN A V upside down.
annotation.definitionFit: Vanilla means plain or ordinary, with no extras.

entries.clue: Musical instrument from India adopted by George Harrison, for example (5)

indicators.note: STAR takes I into its family

blocks.note: a Beatle was a pop star
India is I in the NATO alphabet

annotation.surface: George Harrison took up an Indian instrument, which is exactly what happened.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is true history, since Harrison famously played the sitar, so the clue feels like a general-knowledge question rather than wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: The sitar is a long-necked Indian stringed instrument.

entries.clue: Journey on craft made in three sections (7)

indicators.note: in a down clue, TRIP sits on top of ART

blocks.note: art and craft are both skill

annotation.surface: A voyage aboard a boat built in three pieces.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Craft' suggests a boat to go with 'journey', but it means skill.
annotation.definitionFit: Tripart describes something divided into three parts.

entries.clue: Something to reduce friction, irritation and suffering (6,7)

blocks.note: needle as in annoyance, bad feeling
bearing as in putting up with

annotation.surface: A remedy for rubbing, sore skin and pain.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Friction' tempts you toward interpersonal tension, fitting 'irritation', but it is mechanical friction.
annotation.definitionFit: A needle bearing is a roller bearing with thin rollers that reduces friction between moving parts.

entries.clue: Scottish geologist’s large cry (5)

blocks.note: a yell is a loud cry

annotation.surface: A Scottish rock scientist lets out a big shout.
annotation.walkthrough: The ’s stands for 'is', joining the geologist to his wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: Sir Charles Lyell was a Scottish geologist whose Principles of Geology influenced Darwin.

entries.clue: Numbers is a book of the Bible (4)

blocks.note: numbers as turns in a show
the New Testament book following John's gospel

annotation.surface: A plain statement that Numbers belongs to the Bible.
annotation.walkthrough: Numbers really is a book of the Bible, so the clue reads as a fact; here it means the turns in a variety show.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: a variety-show turn is called a number, and the Acts of the Apostles is a New Testament book.

entries.clue: Pizza from California region (7)

annotation.surface: A pizza from a Californian district.
annotation.walkthrough: The clue reads like a menu description; 'from' simply joins the definition to the two pieces.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the calzone is a pizza folded in half and sealed like a pasty.

entries.clue: Lacking care, like pack prior to game (7)

annotation.surface: Careless handling of a deck of cards before play.
annotation.walkthrough: The first sense is 'not dealt with'; the second is literal, a pack of cards before the deal.
annotation.definitionFit: Something undealt with has had no attention, and a pack before play is literally undealt.

entries.clue: Closely examine artist’s muse’s backside in shock (10)

indicators.note: the back end of a word is its last letter

annotation.surface: Staring hard at a painter's model's bottom causes outrage.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Backside' suggests a nude model, but it only means the last letter.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: behaviour that scandalises people offends their sense of propriety.

entries.clue: Twisted facts and figures slightly (1,3)

indicators.note: the word is turned back to front

annotation.surface: Someone bent the statistics a little.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Twisted' and 'slightly' together sound like mild fiddling of numbers, which hides that 'slightly' is the definition on its own.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: 'a tad' is informal for a small amount, so 'a tad late' is slightly late.
